t: Above you is The Meeting Place, a bronze sculpture about nine metres high and weighing around twenty tonnes. It stands at the south end of the upper level of St Pancras station. It shows a couple locked in an amorous embrace, and it was meant to evoke the romance of travel. It was unveiled in November 2007. It's the work of British sculptor Paul Day, whose high-relief pieces in terracotta, resin and bronze have been shown widely across Europe. His work is known for an unusual approach to perspective.
